o1.biggest_strength: It pairs one flat Agency plan for 8+ channel accounts with an honest yearly-billing fix. It shows low, mid and high revenue cases, a holdout test with three stop rules, and a clear admission that nothing from repricing the base can land inside the board's window.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 'bolder move' on locking yearly prices adds a second idea to a brief that asked for one recommendation. The tables are dense and the text runs to the word limit. The 25-channel cap at $99 may also undercut Team more than the draft admits.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop or shrink the bolder-move section. Spell out the month-6 math more simply so a small team can check it. State what share of Team 8+ accounts would actually qualify for the move-down. Put the yearly-default change on the page as a first-week action with its own expected churn effect.

o2.biggest_strength: It is a tight, readable single recommendation. It has a break-even figure (about 1 in 3 Team 8+ customers moving down), an email that shows each customer's own bill next to the Agency price, and explicit go and stop thresholds. It also keeps the 12-month promise even if the test stops.
o2.biggest_mistake: The base case assumes half of Essentials 8+ customers switch, which is optimistic. The yearly-billing signal is mostly ignored: yearly is offered only at the switch, and the default toggle is never fixed. The 15-channel cap leaves a cliff for the many 8+ accounts near it.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a separate, cheap yearly-default change that ships to everyone. Show a range of cases with the break-even clearly flagged. Test the cap by checking how many 8+ accounts sit above 15 channels. Close the gap between the go and stop thresholds.

reason: Both pick the same right move, a flat Agency plan for 8+ channel accounts. Output 1 also catches the yearly-billing win, gives a proper range of outcomes, and has a sharper holdout test. Output 2 reads more cleanly and has a nicer customer email, but it leaves out the yearly fix and leans on a rosier base case.
